subject: physics
question_text: Express unified atomic mass unit in kg.

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: One unified atomic mass unit is defined as
1/12 of the mass of one atom of the
steps.why: The unit is defined against carbon-12 because that isotope is the agreed standard for atomic masses, so every atomic mass is quoted on the same scale.
common_mistakes: Defining it against a hydrogen atom. The standard is carbon-12.

recall.must_convey: That one unified atomic mass unit is one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.

steps.memory_tip: One twelfth of a carbon-12 atom. The 12 in the name and the 12 in the fraction are the same 12.
steps.margin_note: Write the definition first. The number alone is half the answer.

steps.label: The value in kg
steps.why: The value is close to the mass of one proton, which is a useful check that the power of ten is right.

recall.must_convey: That one unified atomic mass unit equals 1.66 times ten to the minus twenty-seven kilograms.
accept: ten to the minus twenty seven
reject: ten to the minus twenty four

steps.memory_tip: 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg — about the mass of one proton, which checks the exponent.
steps.margin_note: Box the value and keep the kg.

insider_note: Both books ask this. The definition and the number are separate marks — write both, not just the number.
